global_briefing: Analysts should keep three world events in mind. A sharp US tech sell-off weakens AI-linked copper sentiment, though contracted grid demand is slower to fall. China's leverage over antimony, tungsten, and rare-earth export licences stayed central after the Trump-Xi summit, and that leverage shapes Western supply plans. Russian strikes in Poland and rising European defence spending support tungsten and antimony. Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia keep diesel costs a medium-term haulage risk. A US-Canada defence procurement restriction, if confirmed, could affect Canadian critical-minerals sales. Several of these come from single outlets and should be treated as headlines until confirmed.
